papers.title_zh: 哥斯达黎加首次检测到犬瘟热病毒在斑纹松鼠(Sciurus variegatoides)和豪猪(Coendou mexicanus)中的感染
papers.source_body_en: Canine distemper virus (CDV) is a multi-host pathogen capable of infecting a wide range of do-mestic and wild mammals, however, reports of infection in squirrels and porcupines remain scarce. As part of the wildlife rabies surveillance programme in Costa Rica, six wild mammals (four Sciurus variegatoides and two Coendou mexicanus) with neurological signs were evaluated to rule out rabies. All brain samples tested negative for rabies by direct immunofluorescence and RT-PCR. Rapid distemper antigen tests of ocular and nasal secretions were positive in both porcupines, which were subsequently euthanised. Advanced autolysis prevented histopathological evaluation in five of the animals; however, one squirrel showed severe neutrophilic pneumonia with necrosis and haemorrhage, a moderate lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate in the pulmonary interstitium, intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies in bronchial epithelium, and a focal neutrophilic infiltrate in the midbrain. The findings were consistent with CDV infection accompanied by severe systemic bacterial infection. CDV was confirmed in two of the four squirrels and in the two porcupines by RT-PCR and sequencing. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that the Costa Rican sequences grouped into two distinct clusters: one containing both squirrels and another with both porcupines. All four sequences shared a common ancestor with CDV strains detected in domestic dogs in the United States (2012–2013), and more distantly with a dog strain from Argentina (2005). These cases represent one of the few documented occurrences of CDV in squirrels and porcupines worldwide and the first reported in Costa Rica, underscoring the need for continued molecular surveillance to clarify lineage dynamics and spillover pathways.
papers.abstract_zh: 犬瘟热病毒(CDV)是一种多宿主病原体,能够感染多种家养和野生动物,然而,关于其在松鼠和豪猪中的感染报告仍然很少。作为哥斯达黎加野生动物监测项目的一部分,对六只表现出神经系统症状的野生哺乳动物(四只Sciurus variegatoides和两只Coendou mexicanus)进行了评估以排除某种病原体。所有脑组织样本通过直接免疫荧光和RT-PCR检测均未发现该病原体。对豪猪的结膜液和鼻分泌物进行的快速犬瘟热抗原检测呈阳性,随后这些豪猪被安乐死。五只动物因严重的自溶作用而无法进行组织病理学评估;然而,一只松鼠表现出严重的中性粒细胞性肺炎伴有坏死和出血,肺间质中有中度的淋巴浆细胞浸润,支气管上皮细胞中有胞浆内包涵体,中脑区域有局灶性中性粒细胞性浸润。这些发现与CDV感染伴随严重的系统性细菌感染一致。通过RT-PCR和测序确认了其中两只松鼠和两只豪猪感染了CDV。系统发育分析显示,哥斯达黎加的序列分为两个不同的簇:一个簇包含松鼠,另一个簇包含豪猪。所有四个序列都与美国2012–2013年检测到的犬瘟热病毒株有共同祖先,并且与阿根廷2005年检测到的犬瘟热病毒株有较远的亲缘关系。这些病例是全球少数记录的CDV在松鼠和豪猪中的感染案例之一,也是哥斯达黎加首次报告,强调了继续进行分子监测以明确病毒谱系动态和传播途径的重要性。

papers.title: A Disease-Agnostic Data Model and Pluggable Module Interface for Spatio-Temporal Risk Analytics: An Open Reference Implementation Evaluated on Veterinary Surveillance Data
papers.abstract: Spatio-temporal risk analytics for animal-health surveillance relies on established methods—maximum entropy (MaxEnt) suitability modeling, space–time scan statistics, principal component analysis (PCA), and Bayesian prevalence estimation—usually run as isolated, disease-specific workflows. This paper presents a disease-agnostic event schema and a typed plug-in interface, with an open-source Python reference implementation. The full registry-ingestion and modeling workflow was tested with raw anthrax and rabies registries containing 4183 and 363 georeferenced records, respectively. The PCA and Bayesian components, however, used aggregates reconstructed from earlier publications, so those tests assessed interface conformance and numerical reproduction rather than independent validation. With the same inputs, the scan component reproduced the primary SaTScan clusters, yielding Jaccard indices of 0.91 and 1.00, although it matched 8 of 13 significant anthrax clusters overall. Spatial block cross-validation produced produced area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values values of 0.74–0.77 for anthrax, compared with 0.67–0.70 for the elapid MaxEnt implementation; the exact figures depended on fold assignment and regularization. The roughly two-orders-of-magnitude runtime gap also applies only to those particular implementations, feature sets, and datasets. Adding a fifth disease required a single 37-line source loader, with no edits to the 1034 lines of shared code. These results show that the system can run on one workstation, but database-backed deployment, operational scaling, and prospective forecasting were not tested.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to develop a disease-agnostic data model and pluggable module interface for spatio-temporal risk analytics, addressing the challenge of relying on isolated, disease-specific workflows for animal-health surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated an open-source Python reference implementation using raw anthrax and rabies registries with 4183 and 363 georeferenced records, respectively, to test the full registry-ingestion and modeling workflow.
analysis.methods: The system was tested with raw anthrax and rabies registries, and the PCA and Bayesian components used aggregates reconstructed from earlier publications to assess interface conformance and numerical reproduction.
analysis.main_results: The scan component reproduced the primary SaTScan clusters with Jaccard indices of 0.91 and 1.00, although it matched only 8 of 13 significant anthrax clusters. Spatial block cross-validation yielded AUC values of 0.74–0.77 for anthrax, compared with 0.67–0.70 for the elapid MaxEnt implementation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results demonstrate the system's ability to run on a single workstation, highlighting its modular design and potential for integration into existing surveillance frameworks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the system can improve the efficiency and flexibility of spatio-temporal risk analytics for animal-health surveillance, supporting better disease monitoring and response strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study did not test database-backed deployment, operational scaling, or prospective forecasting, and the runtime gap applies only to specific implementations, feature sets, and datasets.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a disease-agnostic data model and pluggable module interface for spatio-temporal risk analytics, with an open-source Python reference implementation. The system was tested using raw anthrax and rabies registries, demonstrating its ability to reproduce SaTScan clusters and achieve moderate AUC values for risk prediction. The modular design allows for easy integration of new diseases, as evidenced by the minimal code changes required to add a fifth disease. However, the study did not evaluate operational scaling or prospective forecasting, limiting the generalizability of the findings. The results suggest that the system could enhance animal-health surveillance by enabling more flexible and efficient risk analysis workflows.

papers.title: Microbiological safety assessment of canine adipose derived mesenchymal stem cell preparations reveal no detectable contamination
papers.abstract: The experimental application of canine adipose-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (cAD-MSC) has demonstrated excellent therapeutic potential in the treatment of a number of previously untreatable or difficult-to-treat diseases. However, the production of cAD-MSC for clinical application necessitates in vitro isolation and cell expansion, introducing the risk of microbiological contamination. Studies indicate that stored MSCs may be contaminated with bacteria, fungi, or viruses, resulting in cell transformation, cell death, or persistent infection. This ultimately compromises therapeutic efficacy and potentially facilitates therapy-induced pathogen transmission. In accordance with the European Medicines Agency guidelines mandating sterility testing as an integral component of the manufacturing process, this study aimed to assess the sterility of the cAD-MSC bank at the Croatian Veterinary Institute. To test for the most clinically significant canine pathogens, nucleic acids were extracted from 32 cAD-MSC preparations and analyzed using standard molecular PCR methods. The pathogen screening panel included rabies virus (Lyssavirus), canine herpesvirus (Varicellovirus canidalpha1), parvovirus (Carnivore protoparvovirus 1), coronavirus (Alphacoronavirus 1), distemper virus (Morbillivirus canis), Rotavirus A, Leptospira spp, Brucella canis, Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato, Anaplasma spp, Ehrlichia spp, Mycoplasma spp (hemotropic), and Neospora caninum. No tested gene fragments of the aforementioned pathogens were detected, indicating that the cAD-MSC preparations were free from the presence of clinically significant pathogens. Rigorous implementation of sterility control during the cell isolation and expansion process is essential to ensure safe cell-based therapy in canine patients.

Studies indicate that stored MSCs may be contaminated with bacteria, fungi, or viruses, resulting in cell transformation, cell death, or persistent infection. This ultimately compromises therapeutic efficacy and potentially facilitates therapy-induced pathogen transmission. In accordance with the European Medicines Agency guidelines mandating sterility testing as an integral component of the manufacturing process, this study aimed to assess the sterility of the cAD-MSC bank at the Croatian Veterinary Institute. To test for the most clinically significant canine pathogens, nucleic acids were extracted from 32 cAD-MSC preparations and analyzed using standard molecular PCR methods. The pathogen screening panel included rabies virus (Lyssavirus), canine herpesvirus (Varicellovirus canidalpha1), parvovirus (Carnivore protoparvovirus 1), coronavirus (Alphacoronavirus 1), distemper virus (Morbillivirus canis), Rotavirus A, Leptospira spp, Brucella canis, Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato, Anaplasma spp, Ehrlichia spp, Mycoplasma spp (hemotropic), and Neospora caninum. No tested gene fragments of the aforementioned pathogens were detected, indicating that the cAD-MSC preparations were free from the presence of clinically significant pathogens. Rigorous implementation of sterility control during the cell isolation and expansion process is essential to ensure safe cell-based therapy in canine patients.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the microbiological safety of canine adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell (cAD-MSC) preparations, as their therapeutic application requires ensuring they are free from contamination that could compromise efficacy or pose risks to canine patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted at the Croatian Veterinary Institute, where 32 cAD-MSC preparations were tested for the presence of clinically significant pathogens, including rabies virus, using molecular PCR methods.
analysis.methods: Nucleic acids were extracted from the 32 cAD-MSC preparations and analyzed using standard molecular PCR methods to detect the presence of the specified pathogens, including rabies virus.
analysis.main_results: No gene fragments of rabies virus or any other tested pathogens were detected in the 32 cAD-MSC preparations, indicating they were free from contamination.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the cAD-MSC preparations met sterility requirements, which is a novel confirmation of their safety for therapeutic use in canine patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide critical information for ensuring the safety of cell-based therapies in veterinary medicine, particularly for rabies virus, which is a significant public health concern in canine populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to testing a specific set of pathogens, and the absence of contamination in the tested samples does not guarantee complete safety, though the evidence is strong given the rigorous testing protocol.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the microbiological safety of canine adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell (cAD-MSC) preparations by testing them for contamination with rabies virus and other pathogens. The research was motivated by the need to ensure the safety of these cells for therapeutic use, as their production involves in vitro isolation and expansion, which can introduce contamination risks. Using molecular PCR methods, 32 cAD-MSC samples were analyzed, and no gene fragments of rabies virus or other tested pathogens were detected, indicating the preparations were free from contamination. The findings suggest that the cAD-MSC preparations met sterility requirements, which is a novel confirmation of their safety for therapeutic use in canine patients. The study's results have important implications for veterinary medicine, particularly in ensuring the safety of cell-based therapies. However, the study is limited to testing a specific set of pathogens, and the absence of contamination in the tested samples does not guarantee complete safety, though the evidence is strong given the rigorous testing protocol.

papers.abstract_zh: 犬脂肪源性间充质干细胞/基质细胞(cAD-MSC)的实验应用已证明治疗对许多以前无法治疗或难以治疗的疾病具有优异的治疗潜力。然而,用于临床应用的cAD-MSC的生产需要体外分离和细胞扩增,从而引入微生物污染的风险。研究表明,储存的间充质干细胞可能被细菌、真菌或病毒污染,导致细胞转化、细胞死亡或持续感染。这最终会损害治疗效果并可能促进治疗诱导的病原体 传播。根据欧洲药品管理局指南,要求将无菌检测作为生产过程的一个组成部分,本研究旨在评估克罗地亚兽医研究所 cAD-MSC 库的无菌性。为了检测临床上最重要的犬病原体,从 32 个 cAD-MSC 制剂中提取核酸,并使用标准分子 PCR 方法进行分析。病原体筛查小组包括狂犬病病毒(狂犬病毒)、犬疱疹病毒(Varicellovirus canidalpha1)、细小病毒(Carnivore protoparvovirus 1)、冠状病毒(Alphacoronavirus 1)、犬瘟热病毒(Morbillivirus canis)、轮状病毒A、钩端螺旋体属、犬布鲁氏菌、伯氏疏螺旋体、无形体spp、埃利希体属、支原体属(嗜血性)和犬新孢子虫。没有检测到上述病原体的测试基因片段,表明cAD-MSC制剂不存在临床上显着的病原体。在细胞分离和扩增过程中严格实施无菌控制对于确保犬类患者的安全细胞治疗至关重要。

news.content_title: Rabies vaccine hesitancy a recurring topic for NH veterinarians, legislators | News From The States
news.content: Last month, the House Environment and Agriculture Committee recommended reconsidering the contents of a sidelined bill from last session: House Bill 1488 , which sought to increase rabies vaccine exemptions for New Hampshire pets. The bill was sent for interim study by the full New Hampshire House in March and, with the 2026 session closed and the biennium winding down, was no longer eligible for passage. Instead, the committee voted, 10-1, to recommend the topic be addressed in future legislation. That move came as a surprise to some. “Truthfully, we didn’t think it was going to go as far,” said Dr. Jane Barlow Roy, who chairs the legislative committee of the New Hampshire Veterinary Medical Association. That’s because there is broad consensus among veterinarians that the rabies vaccine — which protects against a disease both transmissible to humans and universally fatal — is safe and life-saving. Yet the bill was driven forward by pet owners concerned about the rare but non-zero occurrence of adverse reactions to the vaccine, reflecting the increasing hesitancy around both human and pet shots that is driving the resurgence of some infectious diseases in the U.S. Committee members said at an October work session they wanted to keep the door open to potential future changes to rabies vaccine guidance and ensure the topic is revisited if more information becomes available. But answering some of the questions raised by pet owners and legislators, veterinarians said, will require research that is complicated and ethically fraught. A lethal disease For household dogs, cats and ferrets, rabies is the only vaccine required by New Hampshire state law. The viral illness is transmitted when saliva from an infected animal touches broken skin or mucous membranes like those inside the mouth, nose and eyes. The virus moves slowly through nervous tissue, incubating for weeks or more before symptoms like fever, headache, confusion, vomiting, and, later, aggression, difficulty swallowing or paralysis begin to manifest. While post-exposure treatment can prevent the disease from progressing if it is administered soon enough, once symptoms appear, the disease is considered incurable. Wildlife are the most common transmitters of rabies in the U.S., where the prevalence of vaccines has reduced both the disease’s incidence in domestic animals and the rabies death rate in humans and pets. But globally, about 70,000 people die of rabies each year, and more than 99% of people who get the disease outside the U.S. are infected by a dog , according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. In the U.S., there was an unusually high number of human exposures documented this year, according to the CDC. And recent research suggests that the disease is responsible for more human deaths nationwide than scientists once believed. Hesitancy Kelly Arsenault, a Sandown Realtor, is skeptical about some vaccines. But rabies, she said, is not one that she skips when she brings her small dogs to the vet. “I believe in the ability of the body to heal,” she said. “However, rabies is not one of them — and I know that — it is not one of those that the body is going to heal from.” Yet Arsenault, who has for years worked to help rehome and rescue small dogs, also has questions about the rabies vaccine. More than 150 dogs, most of them fluffy and weighing under 15 pounds, have passed through Arsenault’s care over the years, she said. To date, one that she is aware of has had a significant negative reaction to a vaccine, she said, becoming severely ill after injection. Treating the dog with allergy medication managed the reaction, she said, but it was unsettling. She wonders why it happened and whether the incident could have been prevented. Negative reactions to vaccines in pets are uncommon, but most often appear similar to what many people experience after a flu shot, like injection site soreness and mild discomfort, said Dr. Lisa Boyer, a Seacoast area veterinarian, in an online seminar this October. Less commonly, severe reactions can involve facial swelling, vomiting or difficulty breathing. These reactions are managed with veterinary care, said Barlow Roy. And in New Hampshire, as in some other states, a pathway exists in state law to allow owners of pets susceptible to reactions to seek an exemption from the requirement. “The process is there for those dogs and cats that truly should not be getting the rabies vaccine,” said Barlow Roy. That exemption must be approved by the New Hampshire state veterinarian; after it is granted, exempt animals must be kept away from other animals or muzzled. Owners also assume more liability for their unvaccinated animals. For these reasons and the lethal nature of the rabies virus, the veterinarians consider the vaccine more than worthwhile for almost all pets. Yet the online proliferation of information and misinformation about vaccines has raised more curiosity among pet owners, who are asking more questions and starting conversations the veterinarians said they welcomed. However, in some cases, they said, pet owners have also become more likely to push back against professionals’ recommendations. Titer testing HB 1488 sought to broaden the allowed cases for rabies vaccine exemptions in New Hampshire under one condition: A pet has received a series of tests attempting to demonstrate that their immune system has responded to the vaccine. Those tests, known as antibody titers, can measure the level of rabies-specific antibodies, or immune system proteins, in a pet’s blood. The pet’s own white blood cells produce antibodies after they are exposed to the inactivated virus molecules in a vaccine; then the antibodies remain in the pet’s blood, ready to raise the alarm if they ever encounter the rabies virus again, such as if the pet is exposed to rabies from a wild animal. The idea of a titer testing protocol appeals to Arsenault, she said, because if a test could demonstrate that her pet is protected against rabies, she could skip additional “booster” shots. But the problem, according to veterinarians, is that there is currently no test that can prove definitively whether or not a pet has enough antibodies to be protected against rabies. If a titer comes back showing rabies antibodies in a pet’s blood, that confirms that the animal has some degree of immunity against rabies from a previous vaccination, Barlow Roy said. But it takes a certain threshold amount of antibodies to actually combat the virus in the case of a real exposure. That makes the rabies titer test unhelpful for two reasons. One limitation, according to American Veterinary Medical Association President Dr. Jennifer Quammen, is that the test is a snapshot in time of a dynamic situation. The amount of antibodies in a pet’s blood changes as time goes on; this is part of the reason booster shots are called for. Second, scientists don’t have a reliable way of knowing what threshold amount of antibodies a pet’s blood must contain in order for them to be fully protected against the rabies virus. Therefore, in the face of a deadly disease like rabies, veterinarians recommend pets get boosters on schedule to ensure they are protected. An ethical dilemma The limitation of the rabies titer test doesn’t apply to some other diseases for which scientists have developed titer testing protocol. Pet owners may opt to use an antibody titer test to guide decisions about booster shots for some other illnesses, like canine distemper and parvovirus, veterinarians said. With rabies, the factor that has limited the development of a titer testing protocol is the disease’s lethality. Reaching a conclusion about what level of blood antibodies is enough to protect a dog requires testing on living animals. Dogs with different levels of antibodies in their blood, for example, would be intentionally exposed to the disease; some are expected to contract the illness. That result helps scientists determine how much antibody is actually protective. Animals that contract diseases for which treatments exist can be supported after that experiment with medical intervention, Barlow Roy said, making these studies less problematic for investigators. But an animal that begins showing signs of rabies is effectively facing a death sentence, making the protocol more fraught. “We’re not comparing apples to apples, you know? We’re in the same realm,” she said, describing the differences in rabies titer research versus that on other diseases. “It’s more challenging from an ethical point of view ... and that’s why we hesitate,” she said. Arsenault said she was conflicted: While she wants the results of the experiment, she also feels moral qualms about what it would necessitate. “That’s probably where this whole thing gets difficult,” she said. “Would I be willing to be part of that study and watch a dog die from rabies? No ... I don’t know if I could live with myself.” However, some advocates of reducing rabies vaccine frequency have pushed for that research to move ahead, and some studies of limited scope have been completed. That included a 2020 study funded by the Rabies Challenge Fund Charitable Trust that involved the euthanasia of at least 45 beagles, some of which were infected with rabies, raising objections from animal rights groups like People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals. But research has not yielded enough data to draw conclusions, veterinarians told legislators at hearings on HB 1488. Most rabies policy and vaccine guidance is based on a document called the “rabies compendium,” compiled by the National Association of State Public Health Veterinarians. The document is due for revision this year, said Dr. Nathan Harvey, New Hampshire assistant state veterinarian, at an October work session on the bill. Veterinarians expect that the compendium will include updated guidance on the vaccine, possibly — but not certainly — to include guidance around the use of titer testing. “They are looking at whether or not we can start making those correlations to (titer levels) being protective, and that information may come out in the compendium. But we can’t assume that information is going to be published, or not,” Barlow Roy said. The reality at present continues to be that titer tests cannot replace vaccine programs, for the sake of animal and human health, Quammen said. Body size Some pet owners have also raised concerns about particularly small animals, like the dogs that Arsenault rescues. Some negative reactions seem to occur with more frequency in small animals, Barlow Roy said, though she stressed that they are still uncommon. But while pet owners like Arsenault have asked whether a smaller “dose” of vaccine could be administered to smaller animals, that is misleading, Boyer said. Confusion can arise, she said, because many medications are dosed by body weight. But the way that vaccines work — by triggering an immune response — is not as sensitive to body size, meaning that the amount of a vaccine’s active ingredient that an animal must receive for the vaccine to work is not necessarily different for, say, a Pomeranian and a Lab. “If you cut the dose in half and assume you have an appropriate dose, you will not be fully vaccinated or fully protected,” she said. But there are other components besides dead viral molecules in a vaccine, and some formulations exist that deliver the same amount of active ingredient in a smaller volume, Boyer said. It results in death 100% of the time. I think that’s why we are so adamant about rabies and this whole titer discussion.”

news.content_title: 狂犬病未来的发展与面临的挑战(一)引言+流行病学_腾讯新闻
news.content: 前记 : 目前国际上关于狂犬病研究最权威、最全面的大型学术专著是 《 狂犬病的科学基础和管控( RABIES: SCIENTIFIC BASIS OF THE DISEASE AND ITS MANAGEMENT) 》,简称《 狂犬病 (RABIES) 》。该专著最新版( 第 5 版 )已于 2025年7月 面世。 本公众号已陆续将该专著第 4版(2020年版)的绝大部分内容翻译成中文。该专著最新版对旧版有较多更新和改进。本公众号将继续全文翻译该专著最新版的内容,将优先翻译新增加或更新较多章节的内容。 以下为该专著最新版的第 21章: ( Future developments and challenges ) 作者: Anthony R. Fooks 1 , Alan C. Jackson 2 1 Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA), Weybridge, Surrey, United Kingdom ( 英国萨里郡韦布里奇 , 动物与植物卫生管理局 ) 2 Department of Clinical Neurosciences (Neurology), Cumming School of Medicine, University of Calgary, Calgary, AB, Canada ( 加拿大阿尔伯塔省卡尔加里 , 临床神经科学系,坎明医学院,卡尔加里大学 ) 本章目录: 21.1 引言 21.2 流行病学 21.3 免疫学 21.4 发病机制 21.5 动物狂犬病 21.6 动物狂犬病的控制 21.7 人狂犬病 21.8 人狂犬病的控制 21.9 人狂犬病的治疗 21.10 结论 参考文献 狂犬病是一种古老的疾病,至今仍是人类已知最古老的传染病之一 ,并作为 21 世纪最令人恐惧的病毒性人畜共患病之一持续存在。该病的病死率接近 100% ,威胁着全世界贫困人口的生存 (Bannazadeh Baghi and Rupprecht, 2021) 。 犬是狂犬病最重要的储存宿主,造成了超过 99% 的人狂犬病病例 。因此,减少犬介导的狂犬病将带来人狂犬病病例的相应下降。由于监测和报告系统不完善,每年实际发生的人类死亡被严重低估 (Franka and Wallace, 2018) 。在世界许多地区,由于卫生保健基础设施薄弱、教育体系乏力,狂犬病是一种被忽视的疾病,始终是一种与无知和贫困相伴的疾病 (Fooks, 2005) 。这种状况令人不满,尤其是 狂犬病完全可以通过接种疫苗来预防 。在许多狂犬病流行国家,狂犬病的管理被其他卫生优先事项所淹没。狂犬病的许多受害者是生活处境不利的儿童。在许多国家,由于没有实验室确认、往往只有狂犬病的临床诊断,人类的该病常被误诊 (Mallewa et al., 2007) 。这些挑战制约了可用于动物(特别是自由游荡犬)狂犬病控制的资金。狂犬病是 " 同一健康 " ( One Health )的最佳例证,集中体现了需要把兽医医学和人类医学这些彼此分离的群体与生态学家和环保主义者汇聚在一起,以制定成功的干预策略 (Nadal et al., 2022; Saleem and Jan, 2024; Tidman et al., 2022) (见第 20 章)。世界若干地区 已证明狂犬病的消除是可行的 ,并且存在在狂犬病流行国家消除由犬传播给人的 RABV 的愿景 (Abela-Ridder et al., 2016) 。尽管控制狂犬病的许多工具已经具备,我们的知识中仍存在众多 " 黑箱 " 。要降低狂犬病造成的人类死亡人数,需要就特定问题开展更多研究。 这最后一章将聚焦于未来的研究工作,以及那些尚未得到解答、仍需集中研究以推进我们对狂犬病认识的问题 。 RABV lyssavirus 是 狂犬病毒属( Lyssavirus )的原型病毒种,与该属另外 17 个成员一道,隶属于 单股负链病毒目( Mononegavirales ) 弹状病毒科( Rhabdoviridae ) (Walker et al., 2022) 。该属成员的数量正在扩大,反映出这类病毒广泛的多样性以及 RNA 病毒在宿主转换方面所拥有的进化优势(见第 2 章和第 3 章)。狂犬病毒属成员在持续变化的格局动态中不断演化,在亚洲和非洲国家尤为突出 (Fisher et al., 2018) ,而 RABV 继续占全球狂犬病负担的绝大部分,这需要我们理解病毒种、宿主与环境之间的相互关联(见第 4 章和第 5 章)。持续的被动与主动监测结合病毒基因测序,对于增进我们对 RABV 传播以及控制狂犬病所需干预策略的认识至关重要,在发达国家尤其如此(见第 5 章)。未来很可能会鉴定出更多的狂犬病毒属成员。更好地理解病毒的进化,以及病毒在翼手目(蝙蝠)宿主与陆生哺乳动物宿主之间的宿主转换,将有助于我们认识狂犬病毒属病毒未来是否可能浮现。 研发能够对新发现的任一狂犬病毒属成员提供保护性免疫的 泛狂犬病毒属疫苗 ( pan-lyssavirus vaccine )以及广谱抗病毒药物,是公共卫生干预的未来之需 。 (未完待续) 本公众号相关文章的链接 权威的大型学术专著《狂犬病(Rabies)》最新版已面世 2020-06-30 一部跨越二十三年的"狂犬病百科全书" 2026-10-03 大型学术专著《狂犬病》2025年最新版的更新 2026-10-19 当代最著名狂犬病专家为学术专著《狂犬病》写的序言 2026-10-21 狂犬病毒的分类学(一) 2026-10-25 狂犬病毒的分类学(二) 2026-10-27 狂犬病毒的分类学(三) 2026-10-29 狂犬病毒的分类学(四) 2026-10-31 狂犬病毒的分类学(五) 2026-11-02 狂犬病毒的分类学(六) 2026-11-04 狂犬病毒的分类学(七) 2026-11-06

Saleem and Jan, 2024; Tidman et al., 2022) (见第 20 章)。世界若干地区 已证明狂犬病的消除是可行的 ,并且存在在狂犬病流行国家消除由犬传播给人的 RABV 的愿景 (Abela-Ridder et al., 2016) 。尽管控制狂犬病的许多工具已经具备,我们的知识中仍存在众多 " 黑箱 " 。要降低狂犬病造成的人类死亡人数,需要就特定问题开展更多研究。 这最后一章将聚焦于未来的研究工作,以及那些尚未得到解答、仍需集中研究以推进我们对狂犬病认识的问题 。 RABV lyssavirus 是 狂犬病毒属( Lyssavirus )的原型病毒种,与该属另外 17 个成员一道,隶属于 单股负链病毒目( Mononegavirales ) 弹状病毒科( Rhabdoviridae ) (Walker et al., 2022) 。该属成员的数量正在扩大,反映出这类病毒广泛的多样性以及 RNA 病毒在宿主转换方面所拥有的进化优势(见第 2 章和第 3 章)。狂犬病毒属成员在持续变化的格局动态中不断演化,在亚洲和非洲国家尤为突出 (Fisher et al., 2018) ,而 RABV 继续占全球狂犬病负担的绝大部分,这需要我们理解病毒种、宿主与环境之间的相互关联(见第 4 章和第 5 章)。持续的被动与主动监测结合病毒基因测序,对于增进我们对 RABV 传播以及控制狂犬病所需干预策略的认识至关重要,在发达国家尤其如此(见第 5 章)。未来很可能会鉴定出更多的狂犬病毒属成员。更好地理解病毒的进化,以及病毒在翼手目(蝙蝠)宿主与陆生哺乳动物宿主之间的宿主转换,将有助于我们认识狂犬病毒属病毒未来是否可能浮现。 研发能够对新发现的任一狂犬病毒属成员提供保护性免疫的 泛狂犬病毒属疫苗 ( pan-lyssavirus vaccine )以及广谱抗病毒药物,是公共卫生干预的未来之需 。 (未完待续) 本公众号相关文章的链接 权威的大型学术专著《狂犬病(Rabies)》最新版已面世 2020-06-30 一部跨越二十三年的"狂犬病百科全书" 2026-10-03 大型学术专著《狂犬病》2025年最新版的更新 2026-10-19 当代最著名狂犬病专家为学术专著《狂犬病》写的序言 2026-10-21 狂犬病毒的分类学(一) 2026-10-25 狂犬病毒的分类学(二) 2026-10-27 狂犬病毒的分类学(三) 2026-10-29 狂犬病毒的分类学(四) 2026-10-31 狂犬病毒的分类学(五) 2026-11-02 狂犬病毒的分类学(六) 2026-11-04 狂犬病毒的分类学(七) 2026-11-06

news.content: Despite plans for a relatively quick sinking, the S.S. United States remained above the waterline until 9 p.m. Nov. 11. News Former passengers witness final voyage of SS United States William Francis Gibbs, the designer of the SS United States, once said of his ship: “You can’t set her on fire, you can’t sink her, and you can’t catch her.” For eight hours, it looked like the ship would live up to the moniker, as crews with Coleen Marine and Okaloosa County attempted to make the SS United States the largest artificial reef in the world. Read more More Coverage State legislators hear constituent needs at delegation meetings Santa Rosa County’s legislative leaders met Monday, Nov. 9, at Soundside High School in Midway. The meeting was an opportunity for constituents to voice their hopes, concerns and needs for the 2027 legislative session, which is set to begin March 2. FWC investigation leads to conviction in hunting lease fraud An FWC investigation into an elaborate scheme targeting Florida hunters has resulted in a conviction and an eight-year prison sentence. Rodney E. Smith, 39, of Georgia, pleaded guilty to four felonies related to fraud and cheating. FDOH-Santa Rosa to host drive-through rabies vaccine clinic The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County (DOH-Santa Rosa) will host a drive-through rabies vaccination clinic for dogs and cats, Friday, Nov. 13, from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m. at Pensacola State College’s Milton Campus. The campus is located at 5988 Highway 90 in Milton. Enter at the second entrance on Highway 90 Westbound and follow directional signs to reach the clinic site. Pensacola hosting watch party for sinking of S.S. United States A new chapter in maritime history is set to unfold along Florida’s Gulf Coast as the legendary SS United States is scheduled to become the world’s largest artificial reef on Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, weather permitting. The landmark project will further establish Northwest Florida as a premier destination for wreck diving and underwater exploration. They saw me cutting and hauling a tree in my front yard, stopped and helped me finish stacking the debris. Small, family owned businesses like these are the backbone of any community, and I am thankful for the help. I will definitely call them for future lawn care needs and recommend you do the same! Shoutout to the ladies at The Boardwalk Shop These ladies are the kindest. We stopped for batteries and they didn’t have any to sell. But the kind lady went to the back office and gave us 2 batteries that she had. They also gave us shell finding tips and clues to find the Mermaid Mailbox! These ladies are a fine example of the Navarre community and one of the reasons we love traveling from Pittsburgh, PA to this beautiful place! Shoutout to Autism Pensacola 2025 Connecting The Pieces Gala Autism Pensacola’s 19th Annual Connecting the Pieces Gala is Thursday, April 10, 2025, at Sanders Beach-Corrine Jones Community Center. The event features a silent auction, music by the Dharma Beats, a walkabout menu-tasting provided by local chefs and restaurants, signature cocktails and a brief program. All proceeds of the Connecting the Pieces Gala support Autism Pensacola’s outreach efforts to serve children and families affected by autism in the local community. Shoutout to Deb’s Coffee Big shoutout to Deb’s Coffee, a fantastic small business with delicious coffee and passionate staff. My husband and I appreciate y’all so much, and the community wouldn’t be the same without you! Shoutout to Momentum Church Pastor Steven Mendez Momentum church. Pastor Steven mendez. Our barbershop was blessed by him this past summer! He actually blessed just about every place here in navarre, We love Steven at the Navarre beach barbershop, were blessed to have him as one of our supporters. Shoutout to Lisa Lisa helped numerous families in the Navarre area with Christmas, including my own children. I’m a single mom working 2 jobs and doing my best. She helped me put on a decent Christmas. Thankful for her. Shoutout to Volunteers Jovana C. wants to express their heartfelt gratitude to the dedicated individual ( man ) who volunteers to cleans the roadsides along 399. Although I don’t know your name, I notice you every morning after my shift, diligently collecting litter with a trash bag. Your efforts truly make a positive impact on our community. Thank you! Shoutout to Espresso Lane and kind-hearted folks Espresso Lane, our beloved local coffee spot, goes above and beyond to make Navarre a brighter, friendlier place. For those enjoying the walking and running paths, Espresso Lane provides free, refreshing filtered ice water to keep everyone hydrated, and they even have a water station for our furry friends! They have also set up a Free Little Library for anyone wanting to grab a book on their stroll. It’s these small, thoughtful acts that make Navarre such a special community. A huge thank you to Espresso Lane and the kind-hearted folks who make our town feel like home! Shoutout to Juana’s Management Shout out to the management of Juana’s for having a Bands for Bands concert that will help out musicians affected by the recent hurricanes. news.title: Raise awareness and proactively prevent rabies. - Vietnam.vn
news.rss_summary_html: Raise awareness and proactively prevent rabies.  Vietnam.vn

news.content_title: Raise awareness and proactively prevent rabies.
news.content: Raise awareness and proactively prevent rabies. Rabies is a particularly dangerous infectious disease caused by the rabies virus, transmitted primarily through the saliva of infected animals, most commonly through bites, scratches, or licking of damaged skin. Once clinical symptoms appear, the disease is almost 100% fatal. However, death from rabies is entirely preventable if people properly treat the wound and receive timely post-exposure prophylaxis. Find Pet Care Sở Y tế tỉnh Cà Mau • 11/11/2026 According to reports, in the first eight months of 2026, the whole country recorded 69 deaths due to rabies. In Ca Mau , so far, one death due to rabies has been recorded in a human in Nam Nghia hamlet, Tan An commune. Regarding animals, the locality has recorded two outbreaks in Trung Cang hamlet, Tran Phan commune and Hamlet 6, Khanh Lam commune. Deaths from rabies serve as a warning about the persistent risk in the community. In particular, complacency after being bitten or scratched by a dog or cat, or coming into contact with an animal suspected of having the disease, can cause people to miss the opportunity for effective preventative treatment. According to Dr. Nguyen Hoang Tuan Anh, Head of the Department of Infectious Disease Prevention and Control, CDC Ca Mau, rabies is particularly dangerous because once the disease has started, there is almost no possibility of cure. Therefore, prevention and proper treatment immediately after being bitten or scratched by an animal suspected of having the disease are crucial factors in protecting people's lives. Discover more Check Symptoms Find Treatments Get Health Tips Given the continued prevalence of rabies, the Ca Mau Health Department is intensifying its communication efforts through various means, from direct community outreach to information disseminated through newspapers, radio, social media, and integrated into disease prevention and control activities. The communication focuses on the dangers of rabies, prevention methods, treatment of dog and cat bites and scratches, and the importance of post-exposure rabies vaccination. Find Pet Care Notably, the Health Education and Communication Department of the Ca Mau CDC organized 40 training courses on rabies prevention and control for health collaborators. This activity contributed to improving the capacity for communication, counseling, and mobilizing people to proactively prevent the disease at the grassroots level. Mr. Tran Hoang Tien, a health collaborator in Hamlet 1A, Phong Hiep Commune, said: After participating in the training, he understood more clearly the dangers of rabies as well as how to educate and guide people on how to handle dog and cat bites and scratches. He continues to share this knowledge with the people in the local area while carrying out his duties. You may also like Lam Dong province strengthens inter-agency coordination in rabies prevention and control. On November 9th, the Central Institute of Hygiene and Epidemiology, in collaboration with the Lam Dong Provincial Department of Health, organized a training session on monitoring and implementing an inter-sectoral health-veterinary cooperation model for rabies surveillance based on individuals bitten by dogs or cats who receive vaccinations. The disease is almost incurable once symptoms appear. Experts warn that rabies has a nearly 100% mortality rate after symptoms appear, while timely wound treatment and vaccination can prevent the risk of contracting the disease. Stricter penalties for allowing pets to roam freely. Rabies, contracted from bites by pets such as dogs and cats, is considered a dangerous disease. In fact, dozens of deaths from rabies are recorded annually in Vietnam after people are bitten by infected dogs or cats. Yet, people continue to let their pets roam freely in public places. Especially during the hot summer months, when temperatures rise, the incidence of rabies in dogs and cats increases, making this disease even more dangerous. In reality, as awareness increases, people tend to be more proactive after being bitten or scratched by animals. Instead of self-monitoring at home or applying unproven folk remedies, many people go to medical facilities for advice and vaccination. Find Vaccines Ms. Huynh Thi Su, a resident of Hamlet 1A, Phong Hiep Commune, said that after being scratched by a cat, she proactively went to a medical facility for advice and rabies vaccination. This is one of the necessary actions to reduce the risk of contracting the disease after exposure. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), if bitten or scratched by a dog, cat, or animal suspected of having rabies, people should immediately treat the wound by thoroughly washing it with soap and plenty of water for at least 15 minutes, then go to a medical facility for risk assessment and post-exposure prophylaxis. Depending on the case, the exposed person may be prescribed rabies vaccine and anti-rabies serum or monoclonal antibodies. People should absolutely not apply leaves, ointments, irritants, or folk remedies to wounds on their own. Inappropriate treatments can increase the risk of infection and are not a substitute for preventive treatment for rabies. Besides proactively preventing the disease in humans, managing and vaccinating dogs and cats is also an important solution to control rabies from the source of infection. Every family needs to ensure their pets are fully vaccinated, manage their dogs and cats, limit letting them roam freely, and proactively notify authorities when they notice any unusual behavior in their animals. The WHO states that dogs are the source of transmission for 99% of human rabies cases; therefore, vaccinating dogs and managing dog populations are crucial measures to prevent rabies from spreading from the source. Find Pet Care You may also like Dr. Nguyen Hoang Tuan Anh emphasized that rabies is dangerous but completely preventable if people and communities proactively implement preventive measures. This includes combining management and vaccination of dogs and cats with raising public awareness and ensuring timely access to post-exposure prophylaxis. Preventing and controlling rabies is not only the responsibility of the health sector but also requires the coordination of local authorities, veterinary services, and the public. Each family proactively vaccinating their pets; each individual acting correctly and getting vaccinated promptly upon exposure will contribute to preventing rabies and protecting their own health, the health of their families, and the community. Taking proactive preventive measures starting today is the most practical way to minimize tragic deaths from rabies, aiming towards the goal of zero rabies deaths. Every family needs to ensure their pets are fully vaccinated, manage their dogs and cats, limit letting them roam freely, and proactively notify authorities when they notice any unusual behavior in their animals. The WHO states that dogs are the source of transmission for 99% of human rabies cases; therefore, vaccinating dogs and managing dog populations are crucial measures to prevent rabies from spreading from the source. Find Pet Care You may also like Dr. Nguyen Hoang Tuan Anh emphasized that rabies is dangerous but completely preventable if people and communities proactively implement preventive measures. This includes combining management and vaccination of dogs and cats with raising public awareness and ensuring timely access to post-exposure prophylaxis. Preventing and controlling rabies is not only the responsibility of the health sector but also requires the coordination of local authorities, veterinary services, and the public. Each family proactively vaccinating their pets; each individual acting correctly and getting vaccinated promptly upon exposure will contribute to preventing rabies and protecting their own health, the health of their families, and the community. Taking proactive preventive measures starting today is the most practical way to minimize tragic deaths from rabies, aiming towards the goal of zero rabies deaths. news.content_zh: Vietnam.vn 于 2026 年 11 月 11 日发表的文章强调了越南金瓯省持续存在的 狂犬病 风险。报告称,2026 年前 8 个月,全国共记录了 69 例与 狂犬病 相关的死亡,其中当地报告了 1 例人类死亡和 2 例动物 狂犬病 死亡。狂犬病 被描述为一旦出现症状几乎 100% 致命,但通过适当的伤口 治疗 和及时的 暴露后预防 是完全可以预防的。金瓯市卫生局正在通过社区外展、培训课程和媒体宣传活动积极提高人们的认识。金瓯市疾病预防控制中心主任 Nguyen Hoang Tuan Anh 强调预防和正确 治疗 的重要性。文章还指出,人们越来越多地在动物咬伤后寻求医疗建议和 疫苗接种,而不是使用未经证实的民间疗法。专家警告说,狂犬病 仍然是一个重大的公共卫生威胁,99% 的人类病例中,狗是 传播 的主要来源。文章呼吁加强宠物管理、狂犬病和社区教育,以降低狂犬病的风险,实现狂犬病零死亡的目标。

Lifestyle exclusive NYC’s rabies rate is highest in years — and people who feed raccoons are to blame By Ben Cost Published Nov. 10, 2026, 11:10 a.m. ET 2424 Comments See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source 1/1 Skip Ad Continue watchingafter the adVisit Advertiser websiteGO TO PAGE These trash pandas are trouble. New York has been invaded by a plague of rabid raccoons, with Gothamites reporting surging numbers of foaming-at-the-mouth animals across multiple boroughs, sparking fears of infection. According to city data, 2026 has already seen 26 cases spanning the Bronx, Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island, with nearly half the cases at 12. Manhattan, meanwhile, had none (sorry, not sorry). Overall, that’s 30% more raccoon rabies cases than all of last year — and over 12 times the 2024 total. Advertisement While these surges are cyclical, with some years seeing as many as 50, the masked menaces have invaded boroughs where they were previously uncommon. 6 Emergency Service Unit officers use food as a tactic to lure a raccoon into a crate on 58th Street in Brooklyn. Michael Dalton Advertisement “Historically, we never really saw that many rabid raccoons in Queens or Brooklyn,” Sally Slavinski, director of the Zoonotic and Vector-Borne Disease Unit at the New York City Health Department, told the Post. “And then in 2022, and into 2023, we saw clustering of raccoons in Queens along the Nassau County border, and then there was a spread into Brooklyn and into Long Island.” Big Apple residents are feeling the effects. “I reported a sick raccoon in the park by 19th and Hoyt north to 311 that got picked up by park rangers on June 11,” said one Astoria-based Redditor, who said the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene confirmed it was rabid. On September 28, two people in Suffolk County had to receive rabies treatment after their dogs were exposed to raccoons that tested positive for rabies. They were among the 32 cases reported in the county so far this year (up 10% from last year), 31 of which involved raccoons. Advertisement Rabies day out It’s unclear what’s driving the spread of the disease, which primarily passes between raccoons through infected saliva, but Slavinski cited several causes. One is a raccoon boom that’s providing more “opportunities for transmission to occur.” While a population spike hasn’t been confirmed, Long Island notably boasts over 100 of the critters per square mile, compared to just 20–40 in rural areas, Newsday reported. Meanwhile, one longtime Queens resident on Reddit reported a “massive raccoon colony” in Astoria that emerged during the COVID-19 pandemic, although this cluster remains unverified. Advertisement 6 A pregnant raccoon rests near the basement door of A to Z Daycare in Brooklyn, New York. Paul Martinka Meanwhile, Staten Island residents — which boasts 26 rabies cases since 2022 (the second-highest behind Queens at 39) — claimed the critters are “constantly in my yard,” and “there are so many houses going up, they have nowhere to go.” Another possibility is that the virus is fanning out to new areas, exposing trash pandas with little immunity. Slavinski said this can occur naturally or through “translocation events” where people trap and move raccoons to new places. Advertisement In October, a dead raccoon found in an East Islip home tested positive for rabies, prompting Suffolk County to investigate how it got there in the first place, per a county report. Risk factors Contrary to movie depictions, Slavinski notes that raccoons rarely develop “the aggressive form of rabies” that causes animals to chase and bite humans, zombie-style. Instead, rabies-infected raccoons often appear weak or disoriented, and struggle to walk due to creeping paralysis. 6 New York City police officers remove a raccoon on the Upper East Side. Robert Miller Advertisement But it’s still best for people to keep their distance from all raccoons, since on occasion, the ring-tailed dumpster divers might try to attack when they first become sick. Westchester County resident Frank Maida, 81, told The Post about getting mauled in 2019 by a relentless raccoon that later tested positive. “I kept kicking him and he wouldn’t leave me alone,” recalled the senior while describing the infected critter, which reportedly bit multiple people before getting dispatched with a shovel. And even docile Ranger Ricks can transmit the virus to other mammals such as cats, which have a higher animal-to-human transmission rate than raccoons. 6 A raccoon searches for food in a trash can in Central Park in Manhattan. Anadolu via Getty Images Advertisement “When people find a sick cat, they’re more likely to pick it up, bring it to a veterinarian, and that leads to a number of people who potentially get exposed to that cat,” said Slavinski. She noted that cats are also more prone to “aggression” than raccoons — something anyone with a scratch-happy tabby at home already knows. Avoiding bites is paramount, as rabies is 100% fatal without treatment, per the World Health Organization. It starts with flu-like symptoms, followed by rapid neurological decline that includes hallucinations, thrashing, paralysis, and foaming at the mouth. Vax collector To nip outbreaks in the bud, NYC officials distribute mustard-like packets containing an oral vaccine mixed with fishmeal. Generally deployed in autumn, the critter candy is either scattered by hand or hidden inside specialized inoculation stations in public parks and other raccoon hotspots. Advertisement 6 NYPD officers attempt to capture a raccoon on the subway tracks in Brooklyn. Stephen Yang The trick, said Slavinski, is figuring out how to get the oral vaccine straight to raccoons instead of dogs or feral cats. That’s tricky in Manhattan and Brooklyn, but goes more smoothly in Staten Island, where officials can cover large tracts by helicopter, where a wildlife official can toss bait over a known raccoon habitat. Slavinski said the unconventional methods are proven public health savers. For instance, following the 2010 rabies outbreak in Central Park, Slavinski’s team embarked on a vaccination project that essentially “eliminated raccoon rabies from Manhattan.” Individual measures Despite precautions, Slavinski doesn’t see raccoon rabies going away “anytime soon.” Advertisement “As long as we have raccoons, it’s going to continue to circulate until we find a way to produce an amazing vaccine that allows us to vaccinate a really large proportion of that population,” she said. Still, much like Smoky Bear and his forest fires spiel, individual New Yorkers can do a lot to prevent rabies in the Big Apple. Individuals can do their part by reporting sick, potentially infected animals—including those that appear confused or are dragging their hind legs — to 311. 6 A raccoon searches for food in a trash can in Central Park. Anadolu via Getty Images Advertisement And if the animal is behaving aggressively or has actually bitten someone? Call 911 stat and ensure the affected human is receiving immediate medical attention. In an October vaccination announcement, the NYC Department of Health advised New Yorkers to keep garbage tightly sealed and refrain from leaving pet food outdoors, as this can attract raccoons to residential areas. 24 What do you think? Post a comment. And don’t, under any circumstances, interact with raccoons or feed them, even if you’re convinced you’ve encountered Jimothy himself. Lifestyle exclusive NYC’s rabies rate is highest in years — and people who feed raccoons are to blame By Ben Cost Published Nov. 10, 2026, 11:10 a.m. ET 2424 Comments See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source 1/1 Skip Ad Continue watchingafter the adVisit Advertiser websiteGO TO PAGE These trash pandas are trouble. New York has been invaded by a plague of rabid raccoons, with Gothamites reporting surging numbers of foaming-at-the-mouth animals across multiple boroughs, sparking fears of infection. According to city data, 2026 has already seen 26 cases spanning the Bronx, Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island, with nearly half the cases at 12. Manhattan, meanwhile, had none (sorry, not sorry). Overall, that’s 30% more raccoon rabies cases than all of last year — and over 12 times the 2024 total. Advertisement While these surges are cyclical, with some years seeing as many as 50, the masked menaces have invaded boroughs where they were previously uncommon. 6 Emergency Service Unit officers use food as a tactic to lure a raccoon into a crate on 58th Street in Brooklyn. Michael Dalton Advertisement “Historically, we never really saw that many rabid raccoons in Queens or Brooklyn,” Sally Slavinski, director of the Zoonotic and Vector-Borne Disease Unit at the New York City Health Department, told the Post. “And then in 2022, and into 2023, we saw clustering of raccoons in Queens along the Nassau County border, and then there was a spread into Brooklyn and into Long Island.” Big Apple residents are feeling the effects. “I reported a sick raccoon in the park by 19th and Hoyt north to 311 that got picked up by park rangers on June 11,” said one Astoria-based Redditor, who said the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene confirmed it was rabid. On September 28, two people in Suffolk County had to receive rabies treatment after their dogs were exposed to raccoons that tested positive for rabies. They were among the 32 cases reported in the county so far this year (up 10% from last year), 31 of which involved raccoons. Advertisement Rabies day out It’s unclear what’s driving the spread of the disease, which primarily passes between raccoons through infected saliva, but Slavinski cited several causes. One is a raccoon boom that’s providing more “opportunities for transmission to occur.” While a population spike hasn’t been confirmed, Long Island notably boasts over 100 of the critters per square mile, compared to just 20–40 in rural areas, Newsday reported. Meanwhile, one longtime Queens resident on Reddit reported a “massive raccoon colony” in Astoria that emerged during the COVID-19 pandemic, although this cluster remains unverified. Advertisement 6 A pregnant raccoon rests near the basement door of A to Z Daycare in Brooklyn, New York. Paul Martinka Meanwhile, Staten Island residents — which boasts 26 rabies cases since 2022 (the second-highest behind Queens at 39) — claimed the critters are “constantly in my yard,” and “there are so many houses going up, they have nowhere to go.” Another possibility is that the virus is fanning out to new areas, exposing trash pandas with little immunity. Slavinski said this can occur naturally or through “translocation events” where people trap and move raccoons to new places. Advertisement In October, a dead raccoon found in an East Islip home tested positive for rabies, prompting Suffolk County to investigate how it got there in the first place, per a county report. Risk factors Contrary to movie depictions, Slavinski notes that raccoons rarely develop “the aggressive form of rabies” that causes animals to chase and bite humans, zombie-style. Instead, rabies-infected raccoons often appear weak or disoriented, and struggle to walk due to creeping paralysis. 6 New York City police officers remove a raccoon on the Upper East Side. Robert Miller Advertisement But it’s still best for people to keep their distance from all raccoons, since on occasion, the ring-tailed dumpster divers might try to attack when they first become sick. Westchester County resident Frank Maida, 81, told The Post about getting mauled in 2019 by a relentless raccoon that later tested positive. “I kept kicking him and he wouldn’t leave me alone,” recalled the senior while describing the infected critter, which reportedly bit multiple people before getting dispatched with a shovel. And even docile Ranger Ricks can transmit the virus to other mammals such as cats, which have a higher animal-to-human transmission rate than raccoons. 6 A raccoon searches for food in a trash can in Central Park in Manhattan. Anadolu via Getty Images Advertisement “When people find a sick cat, they’re more likely to pick it up, bring it to a veterinarian, and that leads to a number of people who potentially get exposed to that cat,” said Slavinski. She noted that cats are also more prone to “aggression” than raccoons — something anyone with a scratch-happy tabby at home already knows. Avoiding bites is paramount, as rabies is 100% fatal without treatment, per the World Health Organization. It starts with flu-like symptoms, followed by rapid neurological decline that includes hallucinations, thrashing, paralysis, and foaming at the mouth. Vax collector To nip outbreaks in the bud, NYC officials distribute mustard-like packets containing an oral vaccine mixed with fishmeal. Generally deployed in autumn, the critter candy is either scattered by hand or hidden inside specialized inoculation stations in public parks and other raccoon hotspots. Advertisement 6 NYPD officers attempt to capture a raccoon on the subway tracks in Brooklyn. Stephen Yang The trick, said Slavinski, is figuring out how to get the oral vaccine straight to raccoons instead of dogs or feral cats. That’s tricky in Manhattan and Brooklyn, but goes more smoothly in Staten Island, where officials can cover large tracts by helicopter, where a wildlife official can toss bait over a known raccoon habitat. Slavinski said the unconventional methods are proven public health savers. For instance, following the 2010 rabies outbreak in Central Park, Slavinski’s team embarked on a vaccination project that essentially “eliminated raccoon rabies from Manhattan.” Individual measures Despite precautions, Slavinski doesn’t see raccoon rabies going away “anytime soon.” Advertisement “As long as we have raccoons, it’s going to continue to circulate until we find a way to produce an amazing vaccine that allows us to vaccinate a really large proportion of that population,” she said. Still, much like Smoky Bear and his forest fires spiel, individual New Yorkers can do a lot to prevent rabies in the Big Apple. Individuals can do their part by reporting sick, potentially infected animals—including those that appear confused or are dragging their hind legs — to 311. 6 A raccoon searches for food in a trash can in Central Park. Anadolu via Getty Images Advertisement And if the animal is behaving aggressively or has actually bitten someone? Call 911 stat and ensure the affected human is receiving immediate medical attention. In an October vaccination announcement, the NYC Department of Health advised New Yorkers to keep garbage tightly sealed and refrain from leaving pet food outdoors, as this can attract raccoons to residential areas. 24 What do you think? Post a comment. And don’t, under any circumstances, interact with raccoons or feed them, even if you’re convinced you’ve encountered Jimothy himself. Along with rabies, raccoons can carry distemper, bacterial infections, raccoon roundworm, and other illnesses that both humans and pets can catch. And if you thought tainted lettuce was unbearable, a raccoon-borne illness can be infinitely worse. news.content: Skip to main content OKState.edu Quicklinks / Search Close Search Search this site Choose what to search Search this site All of Oklahoma State University Headlines News and Media Open Main Menu Close Main Menu News News Archive Topics Colleges and Divisions In the MediaMagazinesExperts DirectorySubmit NewsContact Us News News Archive Topics Colleges and Divisions In the MediaMagazinesExperts DirectorySubmit NewsContact Us Search Search this site Choose what to search Search this site All of Oklahoma State University Home Articles OSU College of Veterinary Medicine brings veterinary professionals together for annual Fall Conference and World Rabies Symposium Friday, November 13, 2026 Media Contact: Kinsey Reed | Communications Coordinator | 405-744-6740 | kinsey.reed@okstate.edu Share Facebook Twitter Pinterest Key Takeaways Oklahoma State University’s College of Veterinary Medicine hosted its annual Fall Conference and the Boehringer Ingelheim World Rabies Symposium Nov. 5-6. The conference offered continuing education in person and online, covering companion animal, equine and food animal medicine, plus rabies prevention and management. One Health Commission Executive Director Dr. Cheryl Stroud highlighted collaboration across human, animal and environmental health during the Class of 1963 Distinguished Lecture. The rabies symposium covered prevention, treatment and coordinated exposure responses, with hands-on training at the Oklahoma Animal Disease Diagnostic Laboratory. The Oklahoma State University College of Veterinary Medicine welcomed veterinary professionals, researchers and industry experts Nov. 5-6 for its annual Fall Conference, held in conjunction with the Boehringer Ingelheim World Rabies Symposium. The two-day event brought together professionals from across the veterinary and public health fields for continuing education, collaboration and discussions on emerging issues impacting animal and human health. Offered in person at the Roger J. Panciera Education Center and virtually, the conference featured sessions covering companion animal, equine and food animal medicine, along with a dedicated track focused on rabies prevention and management. A highlight of this year's conference was the Class of 1963 Distinguished Lecture, delivered by Dr. Cheryl Stroud, executive director of the One Health Commission. Her keynote presentation, “Foundations of One Health: The Full Scope of the Concept and a Brief Overview of the Global Movement,” explored the importance of a collaborative approach to addressing health challenges that affect people, animals and the environment. A veterinarian with a Ph.D. in endocrine physiology, Stroud brings experience in veterinary practice, industry, academic teaching and research, and One Health advocacy. For 13 years, she has led the One Health Commission, a nonprofit organization dedicated to connecting stakeholders, building cross-disciplinary teams and educating communities about One Health issues around the world. The conference also featured the Boehringer Ingelheim World Rabies Symposium, which brought veterinary, wildlife and public health professionals together to discuss rabies prevention, disease management and the importance of coordinated responses to potential exposures. A featured speaker was Dr. Rodney Willoughby, professor of pediatrics and infectious disease specialist at the Medical College of Wisconsin. Willoughby presented “Curing Human Rabies,” sharing his expertise in human rabies treatment and the Milwaukee Protocol, an experimental treatment approach he developed in Milwaukee in 2004. His presentation explored the challenges of treating human rabies, current therapeutic approaches and emerging research aimed at improving patient outcomes. Additional symposium presentations addressed the National Rabies Management Program, pre- and post-exposure prophylaxis protocols, animal bites and current rabies vaccination issues. Attendees also had the opportunity to participate in a hands-on rabies wet lab at the Oklahoma Animal Disease Diagnostic Laboratory, where participants reviewed proper sampling techniques, field necropsy approaches and sample submission procedures. Dr. Rosslyn Biggs, director of Continuing Education at the OSU College of Veterinary Medicine, said the annual conference provides an important opportunity for veterinary professionals to stay informed and connected throughout their careers. “Fall Conference is one way we continue to support veterinary professionals throughout their careers. Each year, it gives veterinary professionals a chance to hear what’s changing in the profession, talk through cases with colleagues and bring practical ideas back to their teams,” Biggs said. “Offering the conference here at the CVM and online makes it easier for people to participate around the demands of practice.” Biggs emphasized that the rabies symposium demonstrated the importance of the One Health approach and the collaboration needed to protect both animal and human health. “Rabies shows what One Health looks like across veterinary medicine and beyond. When an animal encounters a potentially rabid animal, the veterinary team, diagnostic laboratory and public health officials may all have a role in determining whether people or other animals were exposed,” Biggs said. “The symposium brought veterinary, wildlife and public health professionals together to discuss how they can work together before an exposure occurs and how they can coordinate when one is suspected.” The OSU College of Veterinary Medicine extends its appreciation to Boehringer Ingelheim for sponsoring the World Rabies Symposium and to the speakers, sponsors, alumni and university colleagues who helped make this year's conference possible. “I'm grateful to the speakers, sponsors, alumni and OSU colleagues who made this year's conference possible, and to the veterinary professionals who made time to join us,” Biggs said. Through its annual Fall Conference, the OSU College of Veterinary Medicine continues its commitment to providing meaningful continuing education opportunities and supporting the veterinary professionals who serve communities across Oklahoma and beyond. news.source_body_en: Oklahoma State University’s College of Veterinary Medicine hosted its annual Fall Conference and the Boehringer Ingelheim World Rabies Symposium on November 5-6, 2026, in conjunction with the conference. The event, held at the Roger J. Panciera Education Center and online, brought together veterinary professionals, researchers, and public health officials to discuss rabies prevention, management, and the One Health approach. Topics included rabies prevention, treatment, coordinated exposure responses, and the National Rabies Management Program. Dr. Cheryl Stroud, executive director of the One Health Commission, delivered a keynote on collaboration across human, animal, and environmental health. Dr. Rodney Willoughby presented on human rabies treatment, including the experimental Milwaukee Protocol. The symposium also featured hands-on training at the Oklahoma Animal Disease Diagnostic Laboratory. The event emphasized the importance of interdisciplinary cooperation in addressing rabies-related challenges. No specific outbreak or confirmed cases were reported, and the focus was on education and prevention.

(Photo by Sarah Ladd/Kentucky Lantern) A dog in Acadiana has been diagnosed with rabies, state health department officials confirmed Friday, marking the first canine case of the disease in Louisiana in more than 10 years. Rabies has been relatively rare in Louisiana dogs over the past 20 years, with only five confirmed cases in the state over that time period. The case that the Louisiana Department of Health confirmed Friday is the first in the state since 2014. While rare among dogs, wildlife such as bats and skunks carry the virus and can pass it on to household pets and domesticated animals. It’s spread through bites or scratches from an infected animal. The Louisiana infection comes as rabies cases across the country are on the rise. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention issued a health advisory on Thursday for localities across the country after a spike in rabies cases over the summer, citing increased “reports of animal exposures and rabies post-exposure vaccinations.” Rabies is nearly always fatal to humans after symptoms start, but complications are preventable if the infected person is treated soon after being infected. Fewer than 10 people in the U.S. die from the virus every year, according to the CDC. Most contract the disease from bats, and three of every four Americans live in a community where rabies is present. The virus travels to the brain from an infected wound, with an incubation period of weeks to months before symptoms can begin. Early symptoms include fever, flu-like illness and an itching or prickling sensation at the location of the bite or scratch. Severe rabies symptoms include anxiety, hallucination and intense thirst paired with panic in the presence of liquids. Despite the virus causing near total fatality once it progresses to a late stage, there is a vaccine that prevents rabies from taking hold of both people and animals. People can take additional caution to prevent rabies by avoiding wildlife, vaccinating pets and seeking urgent medical care after being bitten by an animal that could be rabid. Louisiana law requires dogs, cats and ferrets over 3 months old to get a rabies vaccine from a licensed veterinarian. The state has reported an average of six rabies cases in animals each year since 2000, mainly in wildlife. If someone is bitten, scratched or otherwise exposed to an animal with suspected rabies, health officials urge them to immediately wash the wound with soap and water before seeking medical care. news.source_body_en: Louisiana health officials confirmed on September 11, 2026, that a dog in Acadiana has been diagnosed with rabies, marking the first canine case in the state since 2014. This rare occurrence highlights the ongoing risk of rabies, which is nearly always fatal to humans once symptoms appear but can be prevented with prompt treatment. The Louisiana Department of Health noted that rabies has been relatively uncommon in dogs over the past two decades, with only five confirmed cases. The state's case comes amid a national rise in rabies infections, prompting the CDC to issue a health advisory on increased animal exposures and post-exposure vaccinations. Health officials emphasize the importance of immediate wound washing and seeking medical care after potential rabies exposure, while also reminding pet owners of the legal requirement for rabies vaccination. The situation underscores the need for vigilance against wildlife carriers of the virus, such as bats and skunks, which can transmit rabies to domestic animals.
news.content_zh: 路易斯安那州卫生官员于 2026 年 9 月 11 日证实,阿卡迪亚纳的一只狗被诊断出患有 狂犬病,这是该州自 2014 年以来首例犬类病例。这一罕见事件凸显了 狂犬病 的持续风险,一旦出现症状,这种疾病几乎总是对人类致命,但可以通过及时 治疗 进行预防。路易斯安那州卫生部指出,过去二十年来,狂犬病 在狗身上相对罕见,只有 5 例确诊病例。该州的病例发生在全国 狂犬病 感染病例上升之际,促使 CDC 发布关于动物接触增加和接触后 狂犬病 的健康建议。卫生官员强调在可能接触 狂犬病 后立即清洗伤口和就医的重要性,同时也提醒宠物主人注意 狂犬病 狂犬病 的法律要求。这种情况凸显了对病毒携带者保持警惕的必要性,例如蝙蝠和臭鼬,它们可以将 狂犬病 传播给家畜。
